q-108790.name: Question 1
q-108790.worked_solution:
The four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14178390/assets/889b83fadd26b377c4dd34143c9b16541630c04e90de3d9b005e7147ead75ad5.png)

In our case, we are given that $m=3,$ $n=4,$ and $m-r=2.$ 

Substituting $m=3$ into $m-r=2,$ we can find the rank of $A:$

$$
(3)-r=2\,⟹\,r=1
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{dim}(\text{Col}(A)) & =r=1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-108917.name: Question 2
q-108917.problem: Let $A$ be a $m\times n$ matrix. What is the image of $\text{Col}(A)$ under the action of ${A}^{T}?$
q-108917.worked_solution:
First,  notice that ${A}^{T}$ is a $n\times m$ matrix.

Now, pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{m}$ by ${A}^{T}$ gives a linear combination of the columns of ${A}^{T}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ {a}_{1}^{T} & {a}_{2}^{T} & ⋯ & {a}_{m}^{T} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{T}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{m}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{1}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{2}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{m}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{m}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{m}$ under the action of ${A}^{T}$ must be $\text{Col}({A}^{T}),$ the column space of ${A}^{T},$ or equivalently, the row space of $A.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}({A}^{T})$ is mapped to the zero vector $0$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}(({A}^{T})^{T})=\text{Col}(A)$ must be $\text{Col}({A}^{T}).$

This can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14178390/assets/8ca8508d05e28e4c91b5a7f3c65826ce68b5dacd382bfb1a76f09c09d1d004bf.png)

q-109875.html:
Question 5
?

Consider a 4×5 matrix A. If dim(Null(A))=1, then dim(Col(AT))=

a
0
b
5
c
1
d
3
e
4
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The four fundamental subspaces of a matrix A can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

In our case, we are given that m=4, n=5, and n−r=1.

Substituting n=5 into n−r=1, we can find the rank of A:

(5)−r=1⟹r=4

Therefore, we obtain

dim(Col(AT))=r=4.
